references.text: Balak, king of Moab, sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel. This is the original account of the event referred to in Deut 23:5.
Balaam blessed Israel instead of cursing them, as God turned the curse into a blessing.
Balak was angry with Balaam because he blessed Israel three times instead of cursing them.
Nehemiah recounts how God turned Balaam's curse into a blessing for Israel.
Joshua reminds the people that Balak sent for Balaam to curse Israel, but God would not listen to Balaam and turned the curse into a blessing.
Edom refused to let Israel pass through their land and did not meet them with bread and water on the way from Egypt.
The prophet Micah reminds Israel of Balak's plans and Balaam's response, to show the Lord's righteous deeds.
Peter mentions Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness and was rebuked for his transgression.
John mentions the teaching of Balaam in connection with those who hold fast to false doctrine in the church.
